title: One wire contract: JSON bodies, consistent casing, UTC timestamps, explicit content types
iWant: every body, property name, timestamp, and content type to follow one declared convention
soThat: one serialiser configuration handles the entire surface without per-endpoint exceptions

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every request and response body on the versioned surface is JSON; no endpoint accepts or emits form encoding, XML, or bespoke text formats.
acceptanceCriteria.when: request and response media types are enumerated from the generated spec and observed responses
acceptanceCriteria.then: every body media type is application/json or a JSON-structured type such as application/problem+json

acceptanceCriteria.description: Property names follow the project's declared casing (camelCase unless configured otherwise) on every request and response body, with zero mixed-casing endpoints. Applying agent sets: the project-specific bindings, routes, thresholds, budgets, and names named in the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the schemas in the generated OpenAPI spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: every property name is checked against the declared casing rule
acceptanceCriteria.then: no property deviates from the declared casing

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every temporal field is an ISO-8601 timestamp in RFC-3339 form, expressed in UTC with an explicit offset designator.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any response carrying a temporal field
acceptanceCriteria.then: it parses as RFC-3339, is in UTC, and carries the offset designator

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every response, including errors and empty-body statuses, carries an explicit content-type header appropriate to its body.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any endpoint response including 4xx and 5xx paths
acceptanceCriteria.then: content-type is present and correct; no body-bearing response omits it

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request with an unsupported content-type is rejected with 415 and a problem-details body rather than being parsed permissively.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a POST with a body and a non-JSON content-type
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 415 with the declared error envelope

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request with a syntactically invalid JSON body is rejected with 400 and a problem-details body identifying the parse failure, never a 500.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the declared error envelope naming the parse failure
